subject: 2023 Committee Priorities and Specialized Stretch Code
overview: The committee established its operational priorities for 2023 and discussed the potential adoption of the state's specialized opt-in stretch code. Members also reviewed challenges regarding residential heat pump installations and the status of the city's proposed tree ordinance.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the minutes for the January and February meetings.

items.title: Administrative Updates and Resignation
items.summary: Received updates on the expected extension of remote meeting laws through 2025 and announced the resignation of co-chair Gaston Fio.

items.title: 2023 Meeting Schedule
items.summary: Discussed moving the April meeting to accommodate the Mayor's schedule and reached a consensus to continue holding meetings virtually.

items.title: Committee Priorities for 2023
items.summary: The committee identified key priorities including the Harvest Your Energy Festival, tree equity, engaging high school students, and a new initiative for urban meadows.

items.title: Green Energy Awards
items.summary: The committee decided not to resurrect the Green Energy Awards, concluding that the process was labor-intensive and did not effectively promote sustainability.

items.title: Tree Ordinance Update
items.summary: Reviewed the partitioning of the proposed tree ordinance into three parts—public land, private land, and a new committee—ahead of a City Council Committee of the Whole meeting.

items.title: Residential Heat Pump Options
items.summary: Members discussed personal difficulties with the heat pump installation process, citing high electricity costs and conflicting information from contractors.

items.title: Specialized Opt-In Stretch Code
items.summary: Staff presented a comparison between the standard state stretch code and the specialized opt-in version, focusing on HERS rating requirements for new and renovated buildings.
